newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks jump to new highs, eye next records.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks jump to new highs, eye next records.

text.p: Swiss shares staged a record-breaking run, ending at new all-time highs in both the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) and the broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI).
Dealers said the market may continue to break new ground. "We may see 4,000 SMI points in the next few days", one said.

After starting firmer in a technical reactions to Monday's significant losses, the indices were underpinned by a firming U.S. dollar and higher Conf futures. They also gathered strength on the back of rising U.S. bonds and shares.
Blue-chip SMI was up 1.29 percent, or 50.1 points, to 3,924.1.
Broad SPI added 25.35 points, or 1.02 percent, to 2,504.14.
Both indices and several blue chips ended at all-time highs. Dollar-sensitive industrials ABB, Roche and Sandoz and insurer Zurich closed higher than ever.
Roche shot up nearly two percent, or 190 francs, to 10,150. ABB added 23 francs to 1,665. Sandoz was up 13 francs to 1,531 and Zurich added 10 francs to 379.
Most-active Nestle was also among the winners of the day, firming 20 francs to 1,432. SMH registered shares jumped 2.5 percent to 195.75 francs. SMH bearers surged 15 francs to 850.
CS Holding, which suffered heavy losses on Monday, rebounded 2.6 percent to 138.25.
UBS bearer shares added five francs to 1,199.
Utility and industrial group Electrowatt reversed Monday's massive losses, climbing eight francs to 494. Second-tier Motor-Columbus slid farther, losing nearly 1.6 percent to 2,480.

Electrowatt and Motor-Columbus came under heavy pressure on Monday after a major shake-up in the Swiss utilities business. Electrowatt, in which CS Holding has as stake of roughly 45 percent, said it would spin off its utility business under the name of Watt AG. UBS said it would sell two 20 percent stakes in Motor-Columbus to French and German firms.
